gapFill.title: Fill in the gaps
gapFill.subtitle: Type the correct form of the verb in brackets: had + past participle after if, would have + past participle in the result. Twenty original sentences.

questions.before: If I
questions.explain: The past condition takes the past perfect: had + studied.

questions.before: If we had left earlier, we
questions.explain: The past result: would have + past participle. Catch → caught.

questions.before: If she
questions.after: about the party, she would have come.
questions.explain: Past perfect in the if-clause: had + known (irregular participle).

questions.before: If you had asked me, I
questions.explain: Would have + past participle: ‘would have helped’.

questions.before: If they
questions.after: a map, they wouldn’t have got lost.
questions.explain: Irregular participle: take → taken, after ‘had’.

questions.before: If the referee had seen the foul, he
questions.explain: Irregular participle: give → given, after ‘would have’.

questions.before: If it
questions.explain: Negative past perfect: hadn’t + past participle.

questions.before: If I had set my alarm, I
questions.explain: Negative past result: wouldn’t have + been.

questions.before: If he
questions.after: so much, he wouldn’t have felt sick.
questions.explain: Negative past perfect: hadn’t + eaten.

questions.before: We
questions.after: the film if the bus had come.
questions.explain: The result comes first: wouldn’t have + missed.

questions.before: If I
questions.after: my phone, I could have called you.
questions.explain: Irregular participle: forget → forgotten, after ‘hadn’t’.

questions.before: If we had booked earlier, we
questions.explain: Would have + past participle: get → got.

questions.before: If the driver hadn’t braked, he
questions.explain: ‘Hit’ has the same past participle: would have hit.

questions.before: If you
questions.explain: Regular participle: listened, after ‘had’.

questions.before: What would you have done if you
questions.explain: Past perfect in the if-clause: had + lost.

questions.before: If you had won the prize, what
questions.explain: Question form: would + subject + have + past participle.

questions.before: If I had had more money, I
questions.explain: A past ability: could have + past participle.

questions.before: If you had told her the truth, she
questions.explain: A possible past result: might have + forgiven.

questions.before: If Pol
questions.after: to bed earlier, he wouldn’t have been so tired.
questions.explain: Irregular participle: go → gone, after ‘had’.

questions.before: If we had seen the sign, we
questions.explain: Regular participle with a double consonant: stopped.

wordOrder.title: Put it in order
wordOrder.subtitle: Tap the words to build each sentence — 20 examples about a different past, regrets, criticism and questions.

matching.title: Match the base verb and past participle
matching.subtitle: Tap a base verb, then tap its past participle — the form you need after had and would have.

timedMC.title: Beat the clock
timedMC.subtitle: 15 seconds per question. Had + past participle after if; would have + past participle in the result.

questions.text: If I        earlier, I wouldn’t have missed the train.
wrongReasons: ‘Left’ is past simple; a third conditional needs the past perfect.
Never use ‘would have’ in the if-clause.
‘Have left’ is present perfect, not past perfect.
questions.explain: Third conditional: if + had + past participle, ‘had left’.

questions.text: If you had asked me, I        you.
wrongReasons: ‘Would help’ is second conditional (present or future), but this is the past.
questions.explain: Past result: would have + past participle.

questions.text: If she        about the exam, she would have studied.
wrongReasons: ‘Knew’ is second conditional; the result ‘would have’ is past.
questions.explain: Past perfect in the if-clause: had known.

questions.text: If we had taken a taxi, we would have        on time.
wrongReasons: After ‘would have’ use the past participle, not the base verb.
questions.explain: Would have + past participle: arrived.

questions.text: If I had seen you, I would have        hello.
wrongReasons: After ‘would have’ use the past participle: said.
‘Told’ needs a person after it: ‘told you hello’ is wrong.
questions.explain: Irregular participle: say → said.

questions.text: If he had trained, he would have        the race.
wrongReasons: After ‘would have’ use the past participle, not the base verb.
questions.explain: Irregular participle: win → won.

questions.text: If it       , we would have had a picnic.
wrongReasons: ‘Didn’t rain’ is past simple; a past condition needs the past perfect.
questions.explain: Negative past perfect: hadn’t rained.

questions.text: If I had set my alarm, I        late.
wrongReasons: ‘Wouldn’t be’ is second conditional; this is about the past.
questions.explain: Negative past result: wouldn’t have been.

questions.text: I feel sick. If I        so much cake, I’d feel fine.
wrongReasons: The eating was in the past, so use the past perfect.
Present perfect doesn’t work in a conditional if-clause like this.
questions.explain: The past action takes the past perfect: hadn’t eaten.

questions.text: What        if you had lost your keys?
wrongReasons: ‘Would you do’ is about the present or future.
‘Had you done’ is a past perfect question, not a result.
questions.explain: Past result question: would + subject + have + participle.

questions.text: If we had had more time, we        the museum.
wrongReasons: ‘Could visit’ is about now or the future.
questions.explain: Past possibility: could have + past participle.

questions.text: If you had said sorry, she        you.
questions.explain: Possible past result: might have + forgiven.

questions.text: Which is correct in writing?
wrongReasons: ‘Would of’ is just the sound of ‘would’ve’ — never write it.
‘Knew’ is past simple; use the participle.
questions.explain: Write ‘would have’ (or ‘would’ve’) + past participle.

questions.text: In ‘If I’d known, I’d have called’, the first ’d means…
wrongReasons: The first ’d is in the if-clause, where ‘would’ is not used.
questions.explain: In the if-clause ’d = had; in the result ’d = would.

questions.text: If they        the map, they wouldn’t have got lost.
wrongReasons: ‘Checked’ is past simple; use the past perfect.
questions.explain: Past perfect: had checked.

questions.text: If I had known, I would have        to the party.
wrongReasons: ‘Went’ is past simple; after ‘have’ use the participle.
After ‘would have’ use the participle, not the base verb.
questions.explain: Irregular participle: go → gone.

questions.text: If she had studied, she would have        the exam easily.
wrongReasons: After ‘would have’ use the participle, not the base verb.
‘Past’ is a noun/preposition, not the participle of ‘pass’.
questions.explain: Regular participle: passed.

questions.text: If the firefighters hadn’t come, the house        down.
wrongReasons: ‘Would burn’ is second conditional; this is about the past.
questions.explain: Past result: would have burnt.

questions.text: If you        the instructions, you wouldn’t have broken it.
wrongReasons: Here ‘read’ alone is past simple; the condition needs the past perfect.
questions.explain: Past perfect: had read.

questions.text: If he had been careful, he        his phone.
wrongReasons: ‘Wouldn’t drop’ is about now or the future.
‘Didn’t drop’ is a fact, not a result.
questions.explain: Negative past result: wouldn’t have dropped.

errorCorrection.title: Find the mistake
errorCorrection.subtitle: Each sentence has exactly one mistake. Tap the word you think is wrong. Twenty original sentences.

items.message: No ‘would have’ after ‘if’: ‘If I had known…’.
The if-clause takes the past perfect: ‘If you had asked…’.
A past condition needs the past perfect: ‘had left’.
With ‘would have’ in the result, use ‘had known’.
‘Buy’ is irregular: the past participle is ‘bought’.
After ‘would have’ use the participle: ‘gone’, not ‘went’.
After ‘would have’ use the participle: ‘come’.
After ‘would have’ use the past participle: ‘answered’.
The result needs ‘would have’ + participle: ‘would have passed’.
Write ‘would have’, not ‘would of’.
The participle of ‘forget’ is ‘forgotten’.
The participle of ‘write’ is ‘written’.
The participle of ‘take’ is ‘taken’.
Yesterday is past: ‘you would have understood’.
The past condition needs ‘had’, not ‘has’.
Negative past perfect: ‘If it hadn’t rained…’.
The result needs ‘wouldn’t have’, not ‘won’t have’.
Past possibility: ‘could have visited’.
The result question is ‘would you have done’.
Double the consonant: stop → stopped.

levelCheck.title: How well do you know it?
levelCheck.subtitle: 20 mixed questions — typing, word order, past participles, multiple choice and spot-the-mistake. In the typing questions write had + past participle after if, and would have + past participle in the result. One pass, then a breakdown of where you’re strong and where to go back and practise.

items.sentText: If I {{blank}} up earlier, I’d have had breakfast.
If you had come, you {{blank}} it.
If we {{blank}} lost, we’d have arrived first.
If she had worn a coat, she {{blank}} cold.
items.explain: Negative past result: wouldn’t have + got.

items.text: If I had {{blank}} the news, I’d have called you.
wrongReasons: After ‘had’ use the past participle, not the base verb.

items.text: If he had {{blank}} more carefully, he wouldn’t have crashed.
wrongReasons: ‘Drove’ is past simple; after ‘had’ use the participle.
After ‘had’ use the participle, not the base verb.

items.text: If the glass hadn’t {{blank}}, we’d have used it.
wrongReasons: ‘Broke’ is past simple; after ‘hadn’t’ use the participle.

items.text: If you had {{blank}} the sign, you’d have stopped.
wrongReasons: ‘Saw’ is past simple; after ‘had’ use the participle.

items.text: If we {{blank}} the tickets online, we wouldn’t have queued.
wrongReasons: ‘Bought’ is past simple; use the past perfect.

items.text: If she had been free, she {{blank}} us.
wrongReasons: ‘Would join’ is about now or the future.

items.text: If you had been nicer, he {{blank}} stayed.
wrongReasons: After ‘might’ we need ‘have’ + participle for the past.
items.explain: Possible past result: might have + participle.

items.text: If I {{blank}} you were ill yesterday, I’d have visited you.
wrongReasons: ‘Knew’ is second conditional; ‘yesterday’ and ‘I’d have’ show the past.

items.message: No ‘would have’ after ‘if’: ‘If they had come…’.
After ‘would have’ use the participle: ‘taken’.
A past condition needs ‘had studied’.
Write ‘would have’, never ‘would of’.
